summary: First Lady of the United States as the wife of President John Tyler; John's 5th cousin 6 times removed and his one genuine Virginia blood tie.
bio:
Julia Gardiner Tyler was born on 4 May 1820 on Gardiner's Island, East Hampton, New York, the daughter of Senator David Gardiner (1784–1844). In 1844 she married President John Tyler and became First Lady, and she lived thereafter at Sherwood Forest Plantation in Charles City County, Virginia. Her children with the President were David G., John A., Julia, Lachlan, Lyon G., Robert Fitzwalter and Pearl. She died at Richmond, Virginia, on 10 July 1889.

She descends from Bull Smith of Smithtown through Richard Smith 2d; his son Nathaniel Smith (1698–1765), patentee of Moriches, who married Phoebe Howell; Nathaniel's daughter Mary, born 3 October 1725, who married Colonel Abraham Gardiner in 1745; their son Captain Abraham Gardiner (1763–1796), who married Phoebe Dayton; and his son David. That makes her John's 5th cousin six times removed and the one genuine Virginia blood relation in the family. With Anna Symmes Harrison, both First Ladies of the 1840 "Tippecanoe and Tyler Too" ticket are John's cousins, though neither president is.

media.note: Julia Gardiner Tyler (née Gardiner; May 4, 1820 – July 10, 1889) was the first lady of the United States from June 26, 1844, to March 4, 1845, as the second wife of President John Tyler. A member of the influential Gardiner family, Tyler had many figures as suitors.
